case_text:
Vignette:
A 55-year-old man presents with 2 days of bilateral flank pain, initially intermittent but now constant, with associated nausea, vomiting, and markedly decreased urine output over the past 18 hours. His past medical history includes recurrent calcium oxalate nephrolithiasis and gout. On examination, he appears uncomfortable and mildly diaphoretic. Vital signs: T 37.9C, HR 104, RR 20, BP 156/92, SpO2 97%. Bilateral costovertebral angle tenderness is present. Abdomen is soft with mild suprapubic fullness. Labs reveal BUN 68 mg/dL, creatinine 6.2 mg/dL (baseline 1.1), potassium 5.9 mEq/L. Urinalysis shows microscopic hematuria. CT abdomen without contrast demonstrates bilateral ureteral calculi, 8 mm on the right at the ureterovesical junction and 10 mm on the left at the mid-ureter, with bilateral hydronephrosis.
